title: 2D Transforms: Move, Rotate, Scale, Skew 🌀
description: Manipulate elements in two dimensions using `transform` without affecting layout flow.

slides.title: What Are Transforms? 🔄
slides.content:
# Change Shape, Position, and Angle

The `transform` property applies 2D or 3D transformations to an element. It doesn't affect the document flow – the original space is preserved, and the element is rendered on top.

Basic 2D functions:
- `translate(x, y)` – move element.
- `rotate(angle)` – rotate.
- `scale(x, y)` – resize.
- `skew(x-angle, y-angle)` – slant.

You can chain them: `transform: translate(20px, 10px) rotate(45deg);`

quizData.question: `transform: translate(50%, 50%)` moves an element by 50% of its own ______ and height.
quizData.explanation: Percentage values in translate() are relative to the element's own dimensions, not the parent's.

slides.title: Rotate & Scale 🎡
Transform Origin: The Pivot Point 📍

quizData.question: What does `transform-origin: 0 0;` set the pivot to?
quizData.explanation: `0 0` means 0% from left and 0% from top, i.e., the top‑left corner.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Combine Translate with Absolute Centering

`position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%);` is the classic centring trick. The percentages in translate refer to the element's own size.
